Let $P(x,y,z)$ be a variable point on the surface of a cube with edge length 2 centered at the origin. the vertices of the cube lie on the axes. Find the coordinates of the center of the circumscribed sphere as a function of the coordinates $(x,y,z)$ of point $P$.Prove that the sphere is tangent to the axes at the points where they intersect the cube.y



To find the center of the circumscribed sphere, we first need to understand that the circumscribed sphere of a cube is a sphere that passes through all eight vertices of the cube. For a cube with edge length 2, the radius of the sphere is half of that length, that is, 1.

The center of the circumscribed sphere of a cube will be on the line of symmetry of the cube, which passes through the origin and the center of each face of the cube. In this case, the center of the circumscribed sphere is at the point (±half the edge length, ±half the edge length, ±half the edge length) = ±(1,1,1).

So, in general, the center of the circumscribed sphere is at \( C = \left( \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2} \right) \) for any point \( P(x, y, z) \) on the surface of the cube. This center is always in the middle of a face of the cube, but its position relative to the axes is constant.

Let's prove that the sphere is tangent to the axes at the points where they intersect the cube:

To prove this, we need to check if the point \( P(x,y,z) \) on the surface of the cube is exactly one unit away from the center of the sphere \( C \) along the axis.

The distance \( d \) from the center of the sphere \( C \) to any point \( P(x,y,z) \) on the surface of the cube along the axis can be found by considering the projection of \( P \) onto the center of the sphere. Since \( C \) is at \( \left( \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2} \right) \), we need to find the distance from this point to \( P(x,y,z) \). If \( P \) lies on one of the faces of the cube, its projection onto the center will be at a distance of 1 unit from \( C \) along that axis.

We calculate the distance as follows for any point \( P(x,y,z) \) on the surface of the cube:

\begin{align*}
D &= \sqrt{ \left( x - \frac{1}{2} \right)^2 + \left( y - \frac{1}{2} \right)^2 + \left( z - \frac{1}{2} \right)^2 }.
\end{align*}

This distance \( D \) represents the shortest distance from \( P \) to the center of the sphere, and since \( P \) is on the surface of the cube, it will be exactly 1 unit away from \( C \) in the direction perpendicular to the axes. Therefore, the sphere is tangent to the axes at the points where they intersect the cube.



In our proof, what we have calculated the distance with the center of the sphere and points on the surface of the cube, we have figured out that the point in the center of the sphere is exactly one unit away from the points on the surface of the cube when projected.
